name: Godot 4.7.2 is the stable release this handbook targets
summary: Godot 4.7.2-stable shipped 2026-08-18; docs.godotengine.org/en/stable is the 4.7 documentation, and 4.8 is in dev. Version-gate every API claim against it.
detail: Verified from https://godotengine.org/download/archive/ and https://godotengine.org/releases/4.7/ on 2026-09-07. 4.7 itself landed 2026-06-18, 4.7.1 on 2026-07-14. This matters because Godot 3 idiom dominates search results and several 4.x APIs moved inside the 4.x line (EditorInterface singleton at 4.2, @export_tool_button and .uid files at 4.4, EditorDock at 4.6).

name: --headless disables all rendering, so no pixel check can run in it
summary: Godot's --headless is --display-driver headless --audio-driver Dummy; DisplayServer docs state it disables all rendering and window management. Screenshots need a real display server.
detail: Quote: "Starting the engine with the --headless command line argument disables all rendering and window management functions. Most functions from DisplayServer will return dummy values in this case." Offscreen/surfaceless rendering is still only a proposal (godot-proposals#5790) at 4.7.2. A CI pixel lane therefore needs Xvfb plus a software rasterizer (Godot's own godot-benchmarks runs its GPU suite under a headless X11 display) or a GPU runner. Sources: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_displayserver.html and https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/editor/command_line_tutorial.html

name: Input events do not propagate under --headless
summary: Input.parse_input_event() is dropped in headless mode (godot#73557, open since 4.0 RC2), which is why gdUnit4's CLI refuses headless unless you pass --ignoreHeadlessMode.
detail: gdUnit4's command-line documentation states headless is disabled by default "to prevent test errors that inevitably occur during UI tests, since Godot cannot process UI input in headless mode". Consequence for a rebuild: any test that drives real taps or swipes needs either a display server or a seam below Input that gameplay consumes instead of the engine's input singleton. Sources: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/73557 and https://godot-gdunit-labs.github.io/gdUnit4/latest/advanced_testing/cmd/

name: A SceneTree script is Godot's headless harness entry point
summary: godot --headless -s res://tools/x.gd runs a script that must extend SceneTree or MainLoop; SceneTree.quit(exit_code) is what makes CI red.
detail: Documented at https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/editor/command_line_tutorial.html ("-s, --script <script>") and https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_scenetree.html ("void quit(exit_code: int = 0)" — "Quits the application at the end of the current iteration, with the given exit_code"). MainLoop's _process(delta) returns true to end the loop. This replaces Cosmo's vm-sandbox harnesses entirely: no source extraction, no marker pair, no line-number padding — a harness just preloads the class it tests.

name: --check-only parses one script, and script errors may not fail the process
summary: --check-only is documented as "Only parse for errors and quit (use with --script)" — one file at a time. Nothing documents a non-zero exit on a runtime script error.
detail: There is no documented flag that parses every script in a project and returns non-zero. Practical substitutes: run --headless --import once (parse errors surface on stderr), then loop --check-only over each .gd file. godot-proposals#13048 asks for structured headless error output precisely because errors today are unstructured and can drop the process into the interactive debugger, which is a CI hang. CI should grep stderr for SCRIPT ERROR / Parse Error / ERROR: in addition to checking the exit status. Sources: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/editor/command_line_tutorial.html and https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/13048

name: --fixed-fps and --disable-render-loop make a driven run reproducible
summary: --fixed-fps forces a fixed frame rate and "disables real-time synchronization"; --disable-render-loop renders only when script asks. Together they give a deterministic harness clock.
detail: Also useful: --quit-after <n> iterations, --time-scale, --max-fps, --print-fps. Verified at https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/editor/command_line_tutorial.html. Cosmo's harnesses already drive a fixed-step loop (drawcheck plays 2,400 frames); this is the flag set that reproduces that shape in Godot without a browser.

name: RandomNumberGenerator's algorithm is not a stability promise
summary: Identical seeds reproduce a sequence, but Godot's docs say the underlying PCG32 implementation should not be relied on as a permanent detail — so golden tests seeded through it can silently change meaning.
detail: From https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_randomnumbergenerator.html. Practical rule for a rebuild: ship your own small PRNG in GDScript and inject it, exactly as tools/lib/rng.mjs injects a seeded Math into every Cosmo harness today. Prefer xorshift32 over a mulberry32 port: GDScript ints are 64-bit signed and a 32x32 multiply can overflow, so a shift/xor generator is the one that is obviously correct.

name: AudioServer and RenderingServer cannot be stubbed from GDScript
summary: Godot's engine singletons are C++ with no injection point, and neither gdUnit4 nor GUT can double them — so recorded-call harnesses have no direct equivalent.
detail: This is the structural reason Cosmo's three strongest harnesses do not port. musiccheck.mjs stubs AudioContext in a vm and records every oscillator start, frequency and gain write; fxcheck.mjs hands the runtime a fake WebGL context that parses uniform declarations out of the shader; drawcheck.mjs records every 2D call. None of those substitutions is expressible in Godot. The only recovery is architectural: make the decision a pure function that returns typed data, and keep the engine call a thin dumb consumer.

name: gdUnit4 vs GUT: what each can and cannot test
summary: gdUnit4 (v6.2.1, Godot 4.5-4.7.1) has a touch-capable scene runner, C# support and a maintained GitHub Action; GUT (9.7.1) has better doubles and less machinery. Neither runs without the engine.
detail: gdUnit4: extends GdUnitTestSuite, fluent assert_str(x).is_equal(y), CLI addons/gdUnit4/runtest.sh, exit codes 0 pass / 100 failures / 101 warnings, JUnit XML + HTML, refuses headless without --ignoreHeadlessMode. GUT: extends GutTest, assert_eq(a, b, msg), CLI godot -d -s --path "$PWD" addons/gut/gut_cmdln.gd with -gdir/-gtest/-gexit/-gjunit_xml_file, exit 0 pass / 1 any failure. Both lag engine releases, which is a recurring upgrade tax Cosmo does not pay today with harnesses it owns outright. Sources: https://github.com/godot-gdunit-labs/gdUnit4 and https://github.com/bitwes/Gut

name: GDScript warnings as errors are the cheapest harness in the project
summary: debug/gdscript/warnings/<name> takes 0=Ignore, 1=Warn, 2=Error. Setting untyped_declaration and the four unsafe_* warnings to 2 turns a class of runtime bugs into compile errors.
detail: WarnLevel { IGNORE, WARN, ERROR } is verified in modules/gdscript/gdscript_warning.h at the 4.7-stable tag; the 46 live warning codes are in the same file, and the project-setting key is the enum name lowercased (untyped_declaration, inferred_declaration, unsafe_property_access, unsafe_method_access, unsafe_cast, unsafe_call_argument, unsafe_void_return, native_method_override, missing_tool, narrowing_conversion, integer_division ...). Several typing warnings ship as IGNORE because "static typing is optional". Set debug/gdscript/warnings/exclude_addons=true or third-party addons turn CI red. @warning_ignore_start()/@warning_ignore_restore() (4.4+) suppress a region. Source: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/warning_system.html

name: gdtoolkit is the only part of the toolchain that runs without the engine
summary: pip install "gdtoolkit==4.*" gives gdformat and gdlint, which parse GDScript standalone — a fast CI pre-pass, but blind to the engine's type system.
detail: gdformat --check src/ fails on unformatted files; gdlint src/ finds style and shape smells. It does not know class hierarchies or property types, so it finds none of what the unsafe_* warnings find. Run both; they do not overlap. Current PyPI release 4.3.2 as read 2026-09-07. Source: https://github.com/Scony/godot-gdscript-toolkit

name: @tool scripts run in the editor with no undo and no watchdog
summary: Editor-time modifications are permanent, queue_free() during editor logic can crash, an infinite loop freezes the editor, and a plugin script without @tool "acts like an empty file".
detail: All four are stated in Godot's own documentation. The discipline that follows: a @tool script may compute and draw (_draw() writes nothing) but must not start clocks, touch user://, spawn, or free nodes — guard those paths with `if Engine.is_editor_hint(): return`. Enable the MISSING_TOOL warning as an error; it fires on the exact shape of the "acts like an empty file" bug. EditorScript (@tool extends EditorScript, _run()) is the one-shot escape hatch, run from Script editor File > Run. Sources: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/plugins/running_code_in_the_editor.html and https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/plugins/editor/making_plugins.html

name: @export_tool_button replaces the self-resetting bool hack (4.4+)
summary: @export_tool_button("Label") var action: Callable = _method exports a clickable inspector button. Requires a @tool class. Added in Godot 4.4.
detail: Documented at https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/gdscript_exports.html: "If you need to create a clickable inspector button, you can use @export_tool_button. This exports a Callable property as a clickable button." A second argument names an editor icon from the engine's icon set; custom project icons are not supported. Before 4.4 the idiom was an exported bool that set itself back to false in its setter, which is the pattern to stop copying.

name: EditorDock and add_dock() replaced add_control_to_dock() at 4.6
summary: 4.6+ uses EditorDock.new() with title/default_slot and EditorPlugin.add_dock()/remove_dock(); 4.5 and earlier use add_control_to_dock(DOCK_SLOT_*, control). EditorDock is marked experimental.
detail: Verified by comparing the Making Plugins page at /en/4.5/ (add_control_to_dock, remove_control_from_docks) with /en/stable/ and /en/4.6/ (EditorDock, add_dock, remove_dock, EditorDock.DOCK_LAYOUT_VERTICAL). The EditorDock class reference carries the experimental banner: "This class may be changed or removed in future versions." Pin the engine version if you ship a dock. Sources: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_editordock.html and https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/plugins/editor/making_plugins.html

name: EditorInspectorPlugin replaces a number field with a picture
summary: _can_handle(object) plus _parse_property(...) returning true removes the built-in editor; add_property_editor(name, control, add_to_end, label) inserts your own Control.
detail: Signatures verified at https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_editorinspectorplugin.html: _parse_property(object, type, name, hint_type, hint_string, usage_flags, wide) -> bool, plus _parse_begin/_parse_category/_parse_group/_parse_end and add_custom_control / add_property_editor_for_multiple_properties. Register with EditorPlugin.add_inspector_plugin() in _enter_tree() and remove it in _exit_tree(). Every script the editor loads — including the preview Control — needs @tool. Use EditorUndoRedoManager (get_undo_redo()) for any scene mutation.

name: EditorInterface is a global singleton since 4.2
summary: Any @tool script can call EditorInterface.get_resource_filesystem() directly; before 4.2 it was reachable only through an EditorPlugin or EditorScript instance.
detail: The 4.2 change removed the ad-hoc-instance hack that older tutorials still teach (creating an EditorScript just to reach the interface, or threading a plugin reference through every class). Source: godotengine/godot PR #75694, reflected in https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_editorinterface.html

name: Command-line export: import first, and paths are relative to the project
summary: --export-release <preset> <path> needs export templates installed and an export preset; output paths resolve against the project directory, not the working directory. --export-debug implies --import; --export-release does not say so.
detail: Documented at https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/export/exporting_projects.html and the command line tutorial. Run `godot --headless --path . --import` as its own step so the .godot cache exists and is cacheable; the community CI recipe adds `--headless --editor --quit` as a pre-heat when a cold cache makes the first export fail. Templates live at ~/.local/share/godot/export_templates/<version>.stable/ unpacked from the .tpz; 4.7 allows fetching a single platform's templates. --export-pack produces only the PCK/ZIP. Community reference: https://github.com/abarichello/godot-ci

name: What a Godot 4 repository commits and what it ignores
summary: Ignore .godot/, *.translation, export_credentials.cfg. Commit every *.import file, every *.uid file and export_presets.cfg. Secrets live in .godot/export_credentials.cfg, not in the preset.
detail: The import documentation is explicit: "Make sure to commit these files to your version control system, as these files contain important metadata." The export documentation says export_presets.cfg "can be safely committed to version control" while .godot/export_credentials.cfg holds "passwords and encryption keys" and "should generally not be committed". The canonical ignore file is github/gitignore's Godot.gitignore (.godot/, .nomedia, .import/, export.cfg, export_credentials.cfg, *.tmp, *.translation). In CI, cache .godot/imported specifically — not all of .godot/. Sources: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/assets_pipeline/import_process.html and https://github.com/github/gitignore/blob/main/Godot.gitignore

name: UID sidecar files (4.4+) must be committed and must travel with the file
summary: Godot 4.4 generalized uid:// identifiers to scripts, shaders and scenes with .uid sidecars. Gitignoring them makes every clone mint fresh UIDs and breaks scene-to-script references.
detail: They are project state, not build output, and the same rule as .import applies. Moving a script outside the editor means moving its .uid too; the editor then resolves the UID and rewrites referencing scenes on save. For a single-maintainer repository this is low-drama, but it is silent and delayed when it goes wrong. Source: https://godotengine.org/article/uid-changes-coming-to-godot-4-4/

name: .gdignore hides a directory from the whole engine
summary: An empty .gdignore file stops Godot importing or parsing a directory and hides it from the FileSystem dock — but load() and preload() can no longer reach anything inside it.
detail: Quote: "Once the folder is ignored, resources in that folder can't be loaded anymore using the load() and preload() methods." Use it for raw art sources kept beside exported PNGs and for scratch/research directories. Do NOT put a tools/ directory behind it — harness scripts must stay loadable by --script. Source: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/best_practices/project_organization.html

name: What a .tscn diff can and cannot tell a reviewer
summary: Scenes are line-oriented text with a uid header, ext_resource/sub_resource entries and per-node ids — greppable, but a node reorder produces a diff nobody can review as intent.
detail: Header: [gd_scene format=3 uid="uid://..."] (load_steps deprecated at 4.6). References: [ext_resource type="Texture2D" uid="uid://..." path="res://..." id="2_eorut"]. Community folklore says Godot regenerates every resource id on save; there WAS a 4.1 regression doing exactly that (godot#77172) and whether any churn remains at 4.7 is unverified. Read git diff before committing a scene. Merge drivers exist (gdmerge, tscnmerge) but matter little for a single maintainer pushing to main. The practical conclusion is the opposite one: keep content in typed Resource files and code so the review surface stays in .gd and .tres. Source: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/engine_details/file_formats/tscn.html

name: Capturing a frame for pixel regression tests
summary: await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw, then get_viewport().get_texture().get_image() and Image.save_png(). Requires a display server — it returns nothing useful under --headless.
detail: Compare statistically, not exactly: Cosmo's rendercheck already grades edge discontinuity, glow energy ratio, per-world mean/p10/p90 and hue-vs-composition distinctness rather than pixel equality, and that is the right choice across drivers and software rasterizers. Godot has no official screenshot-testing framework; community addons exist (GDSnap) but should be treated as leads. For a frame-exact sequence, Movie Maker mode is the deterministic capture path.

name: Movie Maker mode is Godot's deterministic capture
summary: --write-movie runs the engine non-real-time at a fixed FPS: "faster hardware will allow you to render a given animation in less time, but the visual output remains identical".
detail: Combine with --fixed-fps to pin the rate. This is the right tool for a golden sequence rather than a single frame — an earned drop, a starfall release, a world morph — where one frame cannot show whether the envelope landed on the beat. Output is AVI or a PNG sequence. Source: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/animation/creating_movies.html

name: Performance monitors and viewport render timing, with their limits
summary: Performance.get_monitor() covers frame time, draw calls, orphan nodes and memory; RenderingServer.viewport_get_measured_render_time_gpu() gives GPU ms — but returns 0.0 on Metal and needs rendering.
detail: Enable per-viewport timing with RenderingServer.viewport_set_measure_render_time(rid, true). Several monitors refresh at most once per second ("there may be a delay of up to 1 second between changes"), so sample over seconds. OBJECT_ORPHAN_NODE_COUNT is the cheapest real regression check and it works headless — it catches leaked nodes on teardown. Godot's own godot-benchmarks is the reference pattern: run a scene five seconds, log average per-frame statistics, emit JSON, diff against a baseline. CI on a software rasterizer proves counts, not frame rate; frame rate is a device measurement. Sources: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_performance.html and https://github.com/godotengine/godot-benchmarks

name: Shader.get_shader_uniform_list() is the fxcheck uniform-name equivalent
summary: Loading a Shader and reading its uniform list lets a test assert that every parameter name the game sets actually exists — the typo class that both WebGL and Godot ignore silently.
detail: Signature: Array get_shader_uniform_list(get_groups: bool = false), "Returns the list of shader uniforms that can be assigned to a ShaderMaterial". ShaderMaterial.set_shader_parameter's docs stress the name "is case-sensitive and must match the name of the uniform in the code exactly", and say nothing about erroring on an unknown name. UNVERIFIED: whether the list is populated under --headless, since the dummy rasterizer may not parse the shader — test it, and if it comes back empty run the check in the display lane or fall back to parsing the .gdshader text. Source: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_shader.html

name: Make the Godot arrangement a pure planner so musiccheck's coverage survives
summary: Godot cannot stub AudioServer, so the only way to keep musiccheck's 1,533 lines of arrangement coverage is a pure plan_bar() returning typed note events consumed by a dumb player.
problem: musiccheck.mjs is the only harness that runs the arrangement — smoke, curriculum and drawcheck all run with WebAudio absent — and it works by stubbing AudioContext inside a vm and recording every oscillator start, frequency write and gain write. It is what makes the heard chord sequence assertable (padRoots reads LOG.pad[k*8] as bar k's root), and it pins the pitch law at nine sites, the four-bar chorus seam, the freeze guards, six distinct hooks, voice leading under 12 semitones and the tuned snare at tonic+10. Godot offers no equivalent interception point at any layer.
proposal: Define NoteEvent (at_beat, voice, semitones_over_tonic, gain, duration_beats) with a stable _to_string(). Make Arrangement.plan_bar(level, bar, heat, flags) -> Array[NoteEvent] a static, engine-free function that holds every musical decision. The AudioStreamPlayer layer consumes events and carries no decisions. Then port musiccheck's assertions as gdUnit4 suites over plan_bar output, which run headless in milliseconds and do not need audio to work in CI at all.
risk: A planner that must know wall-clock scheduling state leaks the engine back in; keep the plan in beats and let the player convert. If the drop's landing beat is computed inside the player, the earned-drop timing contract becomes untestable again.

name: Compute shader uniforms in a pure function so fxcheck's value assertions survive
summary: A static SkyUniforms.compute(state) -> Dictionary keeps the uArena/uAccent maths assertable headless, and Shader.get_shader_uniform_list() covers the name-typo half.
problem: fxcheck.mjs asserts uniform names against the shader it was handed (a typo real WebGL ignores silently) and uniform values to 1e-10 — uArena must equal [radiusOf(0)/H, radiusOf(nRings-1)/H, AY] at 2, 3, 4 and 5 rings. Godot's RenderingServer cannot be recorded, and ShaderMaterial.set_shader_parameter is documented to require an exact case-sensitive name but is not documented to error on an unknown one.
proposal: Split the sky uniform block in two. (1) A pure static function taking scene state and returning the exact Dictionary of parameter names to values — unit-testable headless with no viewport. (2) A one-line applier that iterates the dictionary into set_shader_parameter. Add a test that loads the .gdshader, reads Shader.get_shader_uniform_list(), and asserts every key the pure function emits appears in it. Verify first whether that list populates under --headless; if not, this test belongs in the display lane.
risk: If the shader gains uniforms driven directly from a node's _process, the dictionary stops being the whole truth and the test quietly covers less than it claims. Make the applier the only writer.

name: Put a testable seam under Input so the tap/swipe contract stays covered headless
summary: Input events are dropped under --headless, so gameplay should consume a small InputIntent stream produced by one adapter node rather than reading Input directly.
problem: Cosmo's most fundamental player contract is tap always turns, swipe always changes ring, and smoke.mjs:216-266 drives taps, swipes and keys through the real handlers while enginecheck drives real pointer and CDP touch against the built app. In Godot, Input.parse_input_event() is not propagated under --headless (godot#73557, open), and gdUnit4 refuses headless by default for exactly this reason. Without a seam, the entire input surface either needs a display server for every run or goes untested.
proposal: Define a typed InputIntent (turn, ring_up, ring_down, none) and one adapter node that converts InputEventScreenTouch/Drag into intents. Gameplay never touches Input. Unit tests feed intents headless; one thin end-to-end pass in the display lane drives real touch through gdUnit4's scene runner to prove the adapter. This mirrors the typed host boundary Cosmo already has in src/game/contracts.ts, where the scene forwards normalized input rather than the runtime reading the DOM.
risk: A seam that is too abstract loses the gesture tuning — swipe distance thresholds, tap-vs-drag disambiguation — into the adapter, where only the slow lane sees it. Keep the thresholds as data on the adapter and test them as data.

name: Port check.mjs's three routing guards to the Godot repository first
summary: Every harness runs in CI, declares a lane, and is named in the routing document — three text checks over files that need no engine and are the reason Cosmo's suite has not rotted.
problem: The guards exist because the failure already happened: rendercheck.mjs, the only harness in the repository that reads a pixel, was missing from docs/harnesses.md and README.md while both documents asserted fxcheck was the only render-path check. Four harnesses also imported seedLine and never called it for four sessions, so CI's rotating seed never reached the log and every failure was irreproducible. A fresh repository starts with none of these guards and re-earns both failures.
proposal: On day one of the Godot repository, write the static harness that (1) parses the CI workflow for its explicit harness steps and fails on any difference against the harness directory, (2) fails on any harness that declares no lane, (3) fails on any harness not named in the routing document, (4) fails on a seeded harness that never prints its seed. Keep the runner list in the workflow only, and have the local runner read the workflow — never a second list.
risk: None to the game. The only risk is writing it later, after the first harness has already been added without wiring.

name: Ship an owned xorshift32 and forbid global randi()/randf() in gameplay
summary: Godot's RandomNumberGenerator algorithm is explicitly not a stability promise, and global randi() reads a process RNG a test cannot control — so the game should take an injected generator.
problem: Cosmo's determinism today is injected at the sandbox boundary: the game calls Math.random 67 times, every harness passes in a seeded Math, and the seed rotates in CI but is fixed locally so an agent can attribute a changed number to its own diff. Godot has no sandbox boundary to inject at. Using the engine's global randi()/randf() makes runs unreproducible; using RandomNumberGenerator makes them reproducible against an implementation the docs decline to guarantee.
proposal: Ship a ~40-line Xorshift32 RefCounted class (shifts and xors only — a 32x32 multiply overflows GDScript's 64-bit signed ints). Gameplay takes one in its constructor. Add a text guard to the static harness that fails on any \b(randi|randf|randi_range|randf_range|randomize)\s*\( inside the gameplay source directory. Keep the existing convention: SEED from the environment, rotated in CI, printed before the first assertion.
risk: Threading an RNG through every spawn site is friction; the alternative — one autoload holding the generator — reintroduces the global that made it untestable. Prefer construction injection and accept the friction.

name: Budget a second CI job with a real display server for the pixel lane
summary: --headless disables all rendering, so rendercheck's successor needs Xvfb plus a software rasterizer (or a GPU runner) in its own job — and it must load the real art, which no current harness does.
problem: Two problems compound. (1) Godot cannot render headless at 4.7.2; offscreen rendering is still a proposal. (2) Cosmo's existing render coverage grades the art-free path, because tools/lib/game-source.mjs:20 prepends an empty host so getTexture is undefined in every VM harness and in rendercheck; fxcheck asserts uNebulaMap/uPlanetMap/uRingMap are written every frame and passes on a blank texture. Rebuilding the pixel lane without fixing (2) reproduces a hole that already lets a broken art path pass every check.
proposal: A second CI job: install xvfb and Mesa, run `xvfb-run -a --server-args="-screen 0 1080x1920x24" godot --path . --rendering-driver opengl3 --resolution 1080x1920 -s res://tools/harness/pixel_harness.gd`. Keep rendercheck's statistical comparisons (edge discontinuity vs interior, glow energy ratio, per-world mean/p10/p90, no world pair collapsing in both hue and composition) rather than exact-pixel goldens, which are flaky across drivers. Require the real textures to be loaded, and assert at least one manifest key per world is reachable.
risk: Software rasterizer output can differ enough from a phone GPU that a threshold tuned in CI is meaningless on device. Tune thresholds loose and treat this lane as a catastrophe detector, not a taste check. Also unverified for Cosmo: that opengl3 under llvmpipe renders this shader correctly at all.

name: Replace enginecheck with an exported-build boot check plus an honest device checklist
summary: Nothing drives an exported Godot binary from outside the way Playwright drives the built Phaser app, so the shipped-artifact check gets weaker and the documentation must say so.
problem: enginecheck.mjs is the only harness that exercises the shipped artifact: it asserts dist/index.html exists, starts vite preview on 127.0.0.1:4173, blocks every non-GET-to-origin request so no account call or telemetry POST can leave the check, then drives real pointer and CDP touch input and observes COSMO_APP.snapshot() counters. There is no Godot equivalent — no external driver exists for an exported binary — and pretending otherwise is exactly the failure mode the routing guards were written to prevent.
proposal: Export in CI, then run the exported build with --quit-after and a boot-report autoload that prints a JSON snapshot; fail on non-empty error output or a missing/incorrect snapshot. Assert the export produced the expected files. Then write down, in the routing document, that real touch against the shipped build is an on-device manual pass — the same honesty as check.delivery.native-sync, which records that no harness can observe native:sync. Note that the one-scene/one-loop assertion becomes structurally impossible to violate once Godot owns the loop, and OBJECT_ORPHAN_NODE_COUNT covers teardown better than today.
risk: A boot check that only proves the process started reads as coverage to anyone listing the directory. Name what it does not cover in its own header, the way Cosmo's harnesses already do.

name: Turn the GDScript type-safety warnings into errors on day one
summary: untyped_declaration and the four unsafe_* warnings set to 2 (Error), with exclude_addons=true, replace a whole class of what smoke.mjs was invented to catch.
problem: smoke.mjs's own header says it exists to catch "TDZ, load-order, null-deref and typo errors that a parse check cannot". Those are compile errors in a fully typed GDScript project — but only if the warnings are raised, and only if it is done before there is code to retrofit. Godot ships several typing warnings as IGNORE because static typing is optional.
proposal: Commit the [debug] block in project.godot at the first commit: gdscript/warnings/enable=true, exclude_addons=true, untyped_declaration=2, unsafe_property_access=2, unsafe_method_access=2, unsafe_cast=2, unsafe_call_argument=2, unsafe_void_return=2, inference_on_variant=2, plus the bug-shaped ones (unassigned_variable, narrowing_conversion, integer_division, incompatible_ternary, native_method_override, missing_tool, shadowed_variable_base_class, standalone_expression). Use @warning_ignore_start/@warning_ignore_restore (4.4+) for the few engine-boundary clusters. Add gdformat --check and gdlint as a separate no-engine CI job.
risk: Retrofitting later is expensive and tends to end in blanket suppressions. exclude_addons=true is not optional — without it gdUnit4's own code turns CI red. Some engine-boundary calls genuinely cannot be typed; those need explicit, reviewed ignore regions rather than lowering the setting.

name: One editor plugin, for the content tables only
summary: Rings, worlds, powerup pools, formation tiers and level windows become Resource files the inspector already handles; a plugin pays for itself only where a number is not the thing you need to see.
problem: Cosmo's data tables are really content — six level windows against a ten-rung tier ladder, formation shapes as point arrays, orb pools per level. Today their ordering is only ever seen as a pass or a fail (check.mjs:284-285 asserts tier at: values are non-decreasing and level end: values strictly increase; curriculum.mjs drives a real climb). Editing a formation as a list of numbers, or a level window as two integers, is how ordering mistakes get made in the first place.
proposal: Custom Resource classes for every table (free inspector, free typed export, diffable .tres). Then exactly one @tool plugin with: an EditorInspectorPlugin that draws a formation's shape in place of its points array, and a dock showing the six level windows and the ten tier thresholds on one axis. Nothing else — no build or export dock; that is what the command line is for. Note the dock API moved at 4.6 (EditorDock/add_dock) and EditorDock is marked experimental, so pin the engine version.
risk: An editor plugin is a permanent maintenance surface on an experimental API, and every script it loads must carry @tool or it silently acts like an empty file. Scope creep here costs owner time that the game needs. Any scene mutation must go through EditorUndoRedoManager — editor-time changes are otherwise irreversible.

name: Assert counts in CI and frame time on device
summary: Draw calls, orphan nodes and fixed-step process time are stable across hardware and assertable in CI; frame rate on a software rasterizer proves nothing about a mid-range phone.
problem: Cosmo targets 60fps on mid-range phones and has no automated performance coverage at all today — fxcheck pins eight GPU draws per frame and asserts nothing degrades, but no harness measures time. A Godot rebuild can regress draw calls or leak nodes silently, and a naive attempt to assert FPS in CI would produce a number governed by the runner's software rasterizer.
proposal: A perf harness that runs a scripted 5-second run (the godot-benchmarks pattern) and emits JSON: draw_calls_max via Performance.RENDER_TOTAL_DRAW_CALLS_IN_FRAME, orphan nodes via OBJECT_ORPHAN_NODE_COUNT, process time under --fixed-fps, plus render CPU/GPU ms via RenderingServer.viewport_set_measure_render_time when a display is present. Assert budgets on the counts only; record the timings as trend data. Keep frame rate as a device measurement (--print-fps or the remote profiler). Note viewport GPU time returns 0.0 on Metal, so iOS gives nothing here.
risk: A budget tuned on a software rasterizer can pass while the phone drops frames, which is worse than no budget if anyone believes it. State in the harness header that it measures counts, not speed. Orphan-node assertions can be noisy if a framework leaks; scope the count to the game's own tree.

name: Decide deliberately whether drawcheck gets a successor at all
summary: Godot's typed CanvasItem API makes most of drawcheck's bug class unexpressible; the remainder needs a recording draw seam that may cost more than it catches.
problem: drawcheck.mjs records every 2D call and rejects non-finite coordinates, negative radii, unparseable colours, out-of-range alpha, non-positive line width and unbalanced save() across menu, play, landscape and death — requiring at least 200 draw operations per state, because "no violations" is also what a harness that drew nothing reports. In Godot, colours are Color, widths are floats and state balance is the engine's problem; only non-finite coordinates survive as a real bug class, and nothing records calls.
proposal: Do not rebuild it by reflex. Instead: (a) assert finiteness where the geometry is computed, in the pure functions that already need tests; (b) if a recording seam is still wanted, route custom _draw() work through one typed method that a test build can record, and keep the "at least N operations per state" liveness assertion, which is the part that caught a harness drawing nothing. Write down the decision either way so a later session does not re-propose the whole harness.
risk: Dropping it silently loses the liveness check — the one that notices a state stopped drawing entirely — which is the assertion with the highest value per line in that file. If nothing else survives, keep that one.
